title.rendered: Longsuffering: The Fruit of the Spirit | Day 4

content.rendered:
The Greek word for the fourth fruit of the Spirit is makrothumia. It is a compound word. Makros means long. Thumia means temper. Long-tempered. The opposite of short-tempered. The Holy Spirit takes the natural human tendency to explode when tested and, over time, replaces it with something ancient and rare.

The Gospel For Today | Saturday, September 27, 2026 | The Fruit of the Spirit, Day 4

Today’s Scripture

“But the fruit of the Spirit is love, joy, peace, longsuffering, kindness, goodness, faithfulness, gentleness, self-control. Against such there is no law.”
Galatians 5:22-23 (NKJV)

Today’s Message

The Greek word Paul uses for the fourth fruit of the Spirit is makrothumia. It is a compound word, and its two parts open up its meaning completely. Makros means long. It is the same root that gives English words like macro-economics or macro-scale. Thumia, from thumos, means anger, temper, passion, the boiling heat of an emotional reaction. Put them together and you get “long-tempered.” The person whose temper takes a long time to boil. The person who does not explode at the first provocation. The person who is not easily provoked to anger, not quick to retaliate, not shortened in patience by the ordinary friction of life. That is the fourth fruit the Holy Spirit is producing in a believer who has been rooted in Christ. Longsuffering.

The word is used repeatedly in the New Testament to describe the character of God Himself. Peter writes that “the Lord is not slack concerning His promise, as some count slackness, but is longsuffering toward us, not willing that any should perish but that all should come to repentance” (2 Peter 3:9 NKJV). Same word. Makrothumia. God’s temper toward humanity takes a very long time to boil. He has waited generations for people who resisted Him for decades. He waited eighty years for Moses to be ready. He waited for the apostle Paul during years of persecution before knocking him off a horse on the Damascus road. The God the Holy Spirit is bringing us to resemble is a long-tempered God. And the fruit He is producing in us is the same long-temperedness in our relationships with others.

The Passion Translation captures the endurance dimension: “But the fruit produced by the Holy Spirit within you is divine love in all its varied expressions: joy that overflows, peace that subdues, patience that endures, kindness in action” (Galatians 5:22-23 TPT). Patience that endures. Not patience that just survives the day. Patience that endures the season, the decade, the difficult relationship, the recurring frustration, without breaking. The Amplified Bible Classic Edition adds: “But the fruit of the (Holy) Spirit [the work which His presence within accomplishes] is love, joy (gladness), peace, patience (an even temper, forbearance)” (Galatians 5:22 AMPC). Even temper. Forbearance. Not the absence of feeling. The presence of a steadier response.

This fruit is one of the most visible in a believer’s life. The world knows a longsuffering Christian when it sees one. The parent whose child has broken their heart for the fifth time and who chooses to keep loving anyway. The spouse in the long, quiet marriage that keeps choosing to stay. The employee who has been passed over three times and continues to work with excellence. The believer who has been slandered by a fellow Christian and refuses to slander back. That kind of long-temperedness is not a personality trait. It is a supernatural fruit. And in the ordinary friction of ordinary weeks, it is one of the most powerful witnesses of the Holy Spirit’s real work in a real human life.

For Gospelbuzz readers today, this is the fruit the Spirit is growing in you, quietly, week by week. Wherever you are reading this from, in Lagos or London or Manila or Nairobi or Sao Paulo, if there is a person or situation that has been testing your temper repeatedly, do not despair when your patience feels thin. The fruit does not grow in a day. It grows over seasons of yielding to the Spirit, returning to Christ, and refusing to react out of the flesh. The same Holy Spirit who is long-tempered toward you is producing long-temperedness in you. Give Him time. Give Him yielded ground. He will produce it.

Prayer

Father, I acknowledge that longsuffering is a fruit of Your Spirit in my life. You have been long-tempered with me. You have waited for me. You have not exploded at my failures. Today I ask You to produce that same long-temperedness in me, toward the people and situations that have been testing me. I refuse to react out of the flesh. I yield to the Spirit. I trust Him to grow the fruit over the season, not just for the moment. In Jesus’ name. Amen.

Declaration

Longsuffering is the fruit of the Spirit in my life today. My temper takes a long time to boil, because the Holy Spirit is producing in me the same long-temperedness the Father has shown me in Christ.
